name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,541

clue.text: Attractive girl embracing Charlie

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the name wraps its arms around the other piece

blocks.note: a girl's name
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An admiring remark about a pretty girl hugging her friend Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Attractive looks like an adjective praising the girl, but it is the definition, in the sense of instantly appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is one that appeals instantly and sticks, so it is pleasing and memorable.

clue.text: Whitewashes vessels crossing from side to side

indicators.note: the vessels cross the other piece, stretching over it from one end to the other so it sits within them

blocks.note: drinking vessels
as in going over the road, from one side to the other

explanation.surface: Painting a row of pots white, brushing back and forth across them.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitewashes looks like a verb for painting, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a concealment of wrongdoing, so plural whitewashes are attempts to hide the truth, which is what cover-ups are.

clue.text: Explain cut on, say, farm animal? Wire

indicators.note: something cut is trimmed short, so the last letter of the word for explain is lost
in a down clue on means placed above, so the pieces follow one another in the order given

blocks.note: to tell can mean to make known or recount
e.g., for example
a male sheep

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about how to account for a farm animal, then a wire fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a ram is only one example of a farm animal. Wire is the old word for a telegram sent by telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is an informal term for a message sent by telegraph, which is exactly what a telegram is.

clue.text: Lecture supporting His Excellency's ceremonial attire

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits underneath it, so it comes second

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for an ambassador's title
a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speech supporting an ambassador's choice of formal costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Excellency's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A headdress is an ornamental covering worn on the head, often on formal or ritual occasions, so it is ceremonial attire.

clue.text: Quicker way - that's a soldier's style?

blocks.note: first meaning: a more direct route
second meaning, read as two words: the cropped haircut given to army recruits

explanation.surface: Someone finds a faster route and asks whether that is how soldiers do things.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: style means hairstyle, and an army cut is famously cropped close.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcut is a route or method that saves time; split into two words it describes a cropped military haircut.

clue.text: Homer's hard poem going in novel

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Greek poet Homer's difficult epic finds its way into a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer suggests the Greek poet, which the poem in the surface supports, but it is a bird. Novel is not a book here but an adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a racing bird trained to fly back to its loft, the common short name for the bird in the answer.

clue.text: Cross off the sauce, eating fish? On the contrary

indicators.note: eating takes one thing inside another
on the contrary says the eating runs the other way round, so the fish does the swallowing

blocks.note: a flat sea fish
TT, teetotal, describes someone who has given up alcohol; the sauce is slang for drink

explanation.surface: Someone angry about giving up booze while tucking into a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the teetotaller eats the fish; 'On the contrary' flips it so the fish surrounds TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British English for irritable or bad-tempered, so it means cross as an adjective.

clue.text: Carry lion oddly with head in grasp - this will end in tears

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions and drops the rest
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of the two words run together
the opening letter of grasp

explanation.surface: A warning about lifting a lion while holding it by the head: it will go badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This will end in tears' is a stock warning that something will go wrong; read literally, the activity in the answer does end in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping produces tears, so an activity that ends in tears is a cryptic way of describing sobbing.

clue.text: Little child, after change of heart, was first to be named

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and changing it swaps in a different one
after puts the altered child first, with the next piece following

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A small child, having changed their mind, was first to be picked.
explanation.walkthrough: Change of heart sounds like changing one's mind; here it swaps the middle letter of TOT, O becoming I.
explanation.definitionFit: Titled describes a book or person given a title, so as a past participle it means named or called.

clue.text: Coarse fish, with love, thrown back

indicators.note: something thrown back is sent in the opposite direction, so the word for love is read from right to left

blocks.note: a casual spelling of love, as in a term of endearment
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: An angler tosses a rough-looking fish back into the water, with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the love word is reversed; the reversed piece then goes in front of the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and vulgar both describe crude, unrefined behaviour or language, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Stone's thrown at them outside flipping small yard

indicators.note: letters that are thrown are scattered and land in a new order
to flip something is to turn it over, so the abbreviations are read in the opposite direction
the jumbled letters go outside, surrounding the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a stone at people across a little yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone's thrown' reads like a throwing scene, but Stone is the definition and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amethyst is a purple variety of quartz prized as a gemstone, so it is an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Nice lady required me to keep nothing I trade in

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the pronoun wraps around what follows

blocks.note: made, as in compelled: they made me do it
taken as written
the letter shaped like zero
taken as written
to trade in goods is to deal in them, to sell

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper complains of being forced to stock worthless goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the city on the French Riviera, not the adjective; a young woman there would be addressed in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried woman, so it fits a lady from Nice in France.

clue.text: Stiff uniform - daughter's after one

indicators.note: after places one piece directly behind another in the line of letters

blocks.note: a rig is an outfit or costume
the Roman numeral for one
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A school uniform looks starchy, and the daughter is next in line after one sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and rigid both describe something that will not bend or flex, so they are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Doctor anyone can hassle

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that any patient is free to pester the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a noun, the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a bothersome nuisance, and an annoyance is the same kind of irritating trouble.

clue.text: Still footballer - one tries to prevent a shot?

definitions.text: one tries to prevent a shot?

blocks.note: stillness or calm
a goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper standing motionless, trying to stop a shot on goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on shot: the scene suggests a shot at goal, but the answer stops gunfire. Still is a noun here, as in the still of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacekeeper, such as a UN soldier, works to stop fighting breaking out, so they try to keep any gun from being fired.

clue.text: Resuscitate King? Calamitous to rescuer short of oxygen

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the chemical symbol for oxygen is removed
a calamitous event is a disaster that throws things into disorder

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic tries to revive a monarch, but the rescuer runs out of oxygen with disastrous results.
explanation.walkthrough: The oxygen is the O of 'to', removed before the letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To resuscitate is to revive someone or something apparently dead, and to bring back to life is the plain sense of the answer.

clue.text: Shift blame on new fellow who's 8

indicators.note: to shift something is to move it around, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Passing the buck to the newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, TITLED; a lord is a titled man.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman is a man of aristocratic rank holding a title such as earl or duke, so he is a titled fellow.

clue.text: Knowledgeable editor supports European coin

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes last

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European
the ducat is an old gold coin of Europe
the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A well-informed editor backs a single currency for Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: European coin suggests the euro, but the coin is the old ducat and European is just its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An educated person has been well schooled and is well informed, so knowledgeable is a close synonym.

clue.text: Ragbag drags brooms around

indicators.note: letters dragged around are moved all over the place and end up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A scruffy person hauls the sweeping brushes about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragbag looks like a scruffy person doing chores, but it is the definition, meaning a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a motley assortment, and a smorgasbord, figuratively, is a wide and varied mixture of things.

clue.text: Stay up penning the man's dissertation

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word for stay runs backwards
to pen is to enclose, as sheep in a fold

blocks.note: to sit is to stay put
he's, short for he is

explanation.surface: A student stays up late writing a long academic essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay up' reads as staying awake, but up is the reversal signal and penning means enclosing, not writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long piece of research written for a university degree, so it is a dissertation.

clue.text: Grippy thong, to an extent - it squeezes everything tightly

indicators.note: to an extent means only partly, so only a portion of the clue's words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A snug, clinging piece of underwear that pinches everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a tight thong; the definition turns that tightness into a constricting snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a large snake that kills its prey by coiling around it and constricting, crushing it tightly.

clue.text: Magician utters this poetry and she's transformed

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are remade in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the pronoun, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A conjuror speaks a charm and his assistant is changed into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of she's is 'is', so the fodder is just the two words; the magic transformation in the surface doubles as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the exclamation a conjuror says as a trick is revealed, so it is what a magician utters.

clue.text: Detection equipment sub-standard?

blocks.note: first meaning: a system that locates objects by bouncing radio waves off them
second meaning, read cryptically: standard kit on a submarine

explanation.walkthrough: Sub-standard usually means inferior, but the question mark invites reading it as standard on a sub. The answer is also a palindrome, so it reads the same either way down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is the radio-wave detection system used to locate ships and aircraft, fitted as standard on naval craft.

clue.text: Priest absorbed by Roman Catholic memorial

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the priest sits inside the other abbreviation

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A clergyman wholly taken up with a Catholic memorial service.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past and kept in remembrance, so it serves as a memorial or keepsake.

clue.text: Plan to avoid returning after school

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for avoid is read backwards
after puts the reversed piece directly behind the abbreviation for school

blocks.note: a standard abbreviation for school
to elude is to escape or dodge

explanation.surface: A truant's scheme for dodging the journey home after lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or programme of intended events, so as a noun it is a plan.

clue.text: What about this writer, wearing Lieutenant's headgear!

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards
the writer is dressed in the abbreviation, so it sits wrapped inside it

blocks.note: eh? is an exclamation asking what was said
the standard abbreviation for lieutenant
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at the setter turning up in a lieutenant's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Lieutenant's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is a protective hard hat worn by soldiers and others, so it is a piece of headgear.

clue.text: Small pants restricting Republican's bits and bobs

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the underwear word closes around the party letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
pants in the British sense of underwear, informally undies
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Tight underwear cramping a Republican politician's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underpants, not trousers. The 's of Republican's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits and bobs are assorted small items, and sundries are miscellaneous odds and ends of the same kind.

clue.text: High quality of sound after soprano departs

indicators.note: after places the two remaining pieces behind the singer's letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
the tone of a sound is its character or timbre
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: The pitch of the music climbs once the soprano leaves the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After soprano departs' looks like a deletion of S, but soprano gives S at the front and departs gives D at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: High is slang for intoxicated by drugs, and stoned is a slang term for the same state.
